newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-WEEK AHEAD-CPI, wages data seen key for Australian markets.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-WEEK AHEAD-CPI, wages data seen key for Australian markets.

text.p: The focus of the week for Australian financial markets will be the release of third quarter inflation and wages data on Wednesday and Thursday respectively.

While some of the sense of expectation, especially around the wages data, has been lessened by the tough talk in last week's Reserve Bank of Australia Bulletin, economists said the figures are expected to keep the prospect of an interest rate cut firmly on the market's agenda.

Indeed, economists see an almost even chance of a cut in the next month or so. The median percentage of the 32 economists Reuters surveyed on the chance of a rate cut before the end of November was 47.5 percent, with 16 of those surveyed put the likelihood at 50 percent or greater.
Economists, even though who saw a low chance of a November easing, said the odds on a December easing may increase if the activity numbers remain on the soft side through November.

In annual terms the headline rate of inflation is expected to fall to under the underlying rate for the first time since September 1994. The headline rate is likely to fall under 2.0 percent by the end of the year as the impact of two rounds of mortgage rate cuts shows up.
While the headline rate will fall below the underlying rate, the underlying rate will continue to moderate, and it should come in under three percent for the first time since June 1995.

Retailer discounting to clear built up stocks, the benefits of a stronger Australian dollar, low manufacturing sector price increases and a continuing soft labour market are behind the expectations of moderating inflation, economists said.

Average weekly ordinary time earnings (AWOTE) is expected to moderate in annual term to around 3.7 percent, but the potential impact has been lessened by the RBA's expression of concerns over the level of enterprise bargaining agreements and future AWOTE increases.
AUSTRALIAN DOLLAR (Fri US$0.7943/48, New York US$0.7955/60)
The Australian dollar was edging higher at the end of last week, but remained inside its five week long US$0.7855/7965 range.

The pushing back of rate cut expectations, a stronger U.S. dollar, higher oil prices and ongoing demand for high yielding currencies was responisble for the stronger tone, but there are good sellers all the way up to US$0.7960, traders said.
Traders said if a topside break was going to happen next week, it would be before the CPI and wages data, which may see the market become wary of a near term rate cut.

While low inflation is a positive for a currency in that it reflects a well managed economy and improves real yields, it can also be a negative because it can lead to lower rates, especially when the central bank is perceived to be on an easing cycle.
On the downside, support was expected from around US$0.7920, with US$0.7900 expected to prove tough to breach, traders said.
AUSTRALIAN BONDS (Fri 10-yr cash yield 7.60, 3-yr 6.94)
This week is critical for the Australian bond market with the quarterly inflation and wages reports seen by many as setting the scene for a possible reduction in official 7.0 percent interest rates.

However, sentiment in the market will start the week in sharp contrast to last Monday when the preception of a further cut in interest rates around the time of the next board appeared to be nearly a foregone conclusion.

Since then, however, the Reserve Bank has put sufficient doubt in the market place following its quarterly Bulletin, which highlighted the central bank's concern over wages growth and in particularly enterprise bargaining agreements.

Although long bonds have recovered all the losses sustained after the Bulletin, the short-end, and particularly bill futures, are still feeling the after effects since they had been fully factoring in a 50 basis points easing.

The 10-year bond yield has formed a fairly wide range of between 7.50 and 7.75 percent in the past few days, but could break lower if September CPI and underlying inflation on Wednesday and Thursday's August quarter average weekly ordinary time earnings (AWOTE) come in below expectations.

Bond prices are not likely to get much a lead from U.S. Treasuries which ended barely changed on Friday in New York after profit-taking in front of new supply erased early gains. The 6-3/4 percent 30-year benchmark Treasury bond ended at 99-12/32, up 1/32, to yield 6.80 percent, unchanged on Thursday's level.
AUSTRALIAN STOCKS (Fri: All Ordinaries 2,355.0, up 1.2)

Wall's Street climb on Friday to yet another all-time high should encourage investors to take the Australian share market up to record territory again after Friday's retreat. The Dow rose 35.03 to a record 6094.23, the Dow's 31st record closing high for 1996 and the fourth in the week. The blue chip index surged 124.85 points over the week.

Australian shares finished a record-breaking week with profit-taking on Friday. Dealers said the subdued end to the week highlighted the underlying caution felt by the market particularly with the Wall Street market at such high levels.
Dealers said that recent media commentary had suggested the Dow could be near levels which may prompt a significant retracement.
"However, local market sentiment is still good because the feeling is that the Australian market is relatively undervalued compared to other world markets," a Sydney-based dealer said.
"The market is well-positioned to take advantage of any more gains by Wall Street without being too badly affected by a pull-back in that market," he said.

A large number of company's go ex-dividend this week with Wednesday the most affected day with a large number of stocks changing the basis of their quotation including Arnotts Ltd and Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd.

In terms of company news a large number of annual meetings occur this week including ANI Ltd in Sydney on Monday, The Australian Gas Light Co and Wattyl Ltd in Sydney on Tuesday, Normandy Mining Ltd in Sydney on Wenesday, Newcrest Mining Ltd in Melbourne on Thursday and Amcor Ltd in Melbourne and Pioneer International Ltd in Sydney on Friday.
Share market investors like other market traders will be watching Wednesday's release of third quarter inflation data and wages data on Thursday.
Dealers said a sharp movement in reaction to the data by the Australian bond market was likely to be mirrored by the bourse.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
